name: Hatita
title: Temple Gatekeeper After the Exile
summary: Hatita was one of the gatekeepers (doorkeepers) in the temple after the Israelites returned from the Babylonian exile. His descendants are mentioned among those who returned with Zerubbabel to rebuild the temple in Jerusalem. The gatekeepers played an important role in protecting and guarding the sanctuary.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned Among the Gatekeepers Who Returned from Exile
keyEvents.description: Hatita's descendants are listed among the gatekeepers who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel.

keyEvents.title: Listed in Nehemiah's Register of Returnees
keyEvents.description: Hatita's family is again mentioned among the gatekeepers in Nehemiah's register of those who returned from exile.

keyEvents.title: The Gatekeepers Serving at the Rebuilt Temple
keyEvents.description: After returning from Babylon, the gatekeepers, including the descendants of Shallum, took up their posts at the gates of God's house.

keyEvents.title: The Gatekeepers as Part of the Temple Servants
keyEvents.description: The gatekeepers, including Shallum's family, were responsible for guarding the temple entrances and maintaining order in the sanctuary.

keyEvents.title: The Role of the Levites and Gatekeepers in the New Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: After Nehemiah's reforms, the gatekeepers, including the descendants of Shallum, were assigned specific duties and supported by the people's tithes.
